title: King before the pawn
note: Bring your king ahead of the pawn. Use it to control the promotion route before advancing.

title: The opposition
note: Count the squares between the kings. A pawn move changes whose turn it is to give way.

title: The rook-pawn corner
note: The edge removes a route around the defending king. Check stalemate before pushing.

title: Choose a promotion
note: Compare each promotion. A queen has the most power, but every new position needs a stalemate check.

title: A pawn race
note: Count pawn moves and king moves separately. Recalculate after either side gives check.

title: Connected passers
note: Keep the pawns connected. Advancing the wrong pawn can leave its partner without support.

title: Separated passers
note: A distant passer can pull the defending king away. Compare its route to both promotion squares.

title: Black goes up the board
note: From Black’s side, promotion is on the first rank. Use your king to protect the pawn and avoid stalemate.

title: Shrink the box
note: Use the rook to restrict ranks or files, then bring your king closer. Keep the rook safe from the king.

title: Cut off the king
note: Cut the king off with the rook. Improve your king before giving checks that let the defender escape.

title: Rook against a passer
note: Calculate the next promotion before chasing the king. Checks can gain time for the rook to reach the pawn.

title: Rook and pawn teamwork
note: Coordinate the king, rook and pawn. The extra material does not remove the need to check stalemate.

title: Active rooks
note: Rook activity and king safety both matter. Before trading, calculate the king ending that remains.

title: Rook technique as Black
note: Use your rook to make the board smaller for White’s king. Your own king must help with the final net.

title: Finish the queen mate
note: Look for a mating net supported by your king. Distinguish checkmate from leaving the king with no legal move.

title: Leave one square
note: Restrict the king without stalemating it. Bring your king into the net before the final check.

title: Queen against an advanced pawn
note: A pawn on the seventh rank demands exact calculation. Check promotion threats and stalemate resources.

title: Queen versus rook
note: Look for checks that separate the rook from its king. Check whether a capture changes the result.

title: Two bishops working together
note: The bishops cover opposite color complexes. Coordinate them with your king to reduce the defender’s space.

title: Bishop and knight coordination
note: Coordinate all three pieces. The bishop’s color determines which corner can support the final mating net.

title: The wrong bishop and rook pawn
note: Compare the bishop’s color with the promotion square. A king anchored in the corner can change everything.

title: The other color bishop
note: The bishop can control this promotion square. Work with your king to dislodge the defender.

title: Knight against a passer
note: Find the knight’s route to blockade the pawn. A knight may need several moves to reach a nearby square.

title: Bishop against a passer
note: Trace the bishop’s diagonals to the promotion square. The defending king may have to cover squares of the other color.
